To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the σ28‐FlgM regulatory network controls class 3 flagellar gene expression in Salmonella entericaserovar Typhimurium in response to hook‐basal‐body assembly.
the σ28–FgM regulatory circuit controls flagellar gene expression in response HBB abundance in a continuous and dynamic manner.
the σ28‐FlgM regulatory network continuously senses HBB assembly and regulates the timing and magnitude (number) of class 3 flagellar gene expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the σ28– FlgM regulatory circuit controls the timing and magnitude in flagellar gene expression.
understanding how the σ28–flgM regulatory circuit controls class 3 flagellar gene expression.
how a complex biological process is coordinated and controlled.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
σ28‐mediated control of flagellar class 3 gene transcription is continuous, and is dependent on the abundance of HBB.
the σ28‐FlgM regulatory pathway is the key to controlling the timing of class 3 genes expression, which is a critical component of flagellar number control.
the σ28‐FlgM regulatory module acts as a sensor that controls the timing and magnitude (i.e. flagellar number) of class 3 flagellar genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the σ28‐FlgM regulatory network acts as an adaptive control system that continuously monitors and regulates flagellar gene expression and possibly the number of flagella in response to Hbb assembly.
the σ28‐dependent transcription of class 3 genes is continuously regulated by FlgM in response to changes in the abundance of HBB.
this regulatory system acts as a feedback controller to continuously control flagellar gene expression in response the assembly of the flagellar apparatus.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the σ28‐FlgM regulatory mechanism is not just an on‐off switch, but is instead a continuously operating feedback mechanism that controls flagellar gene expression in a manner that is proportional to HBB assembly.
a simple negative feedback loop can be used to continuously control gene expression and that this control can be achieved by rewiring the temporal order of gene expression.
the flagellar regulatory circuit can be used as a model for understanding how the timing of gene expression is controlled by sensing the assembly of macromolecular machines.
